body_html:
How to think about it

Minerals are classified by chemistry: silicates (quartz, feldspar, mica), carbonates (calcite), oxides, sulfides and native elements. They are identified by hardness, cleavage, lustre, streak and specific gravity.

Igneous textures show cooling rate (coarse = slow, fine = fast, glassy = very fast). Sedimentary rocks are clastic (sandstone, shale), chemical or organic. Metamorphic rocks are foliated (slate, schist, gneiss) or non-foliated (marble, quartzite). BC has copper, gold, molybdenum and coal deposits.

Example

Which mineral fizzes in dilute acid?

A carbonate

Answer: calcite

Example

Gneiss has bands of light and dark minerals. What is this texture called?

Layers from pressure

Answer: foliation

Common mistakes

  • Thinking all rocks are made of one mineral.
  • Using color alone to identify minerals.
  • Thinking marble is foliated.

faq.a: Lava cooled so fast that crystals had no time to form.

items.q: How does sediment become sedimentary rock?
c: It is heated until it glows.
Layers are squashed (compaction) and stuck together (cementation).
items.e: Over millions of years.

items.q: What is the difference between weathering and erosion?
c: Weathering breaks rock down where it is; erosion carries the pieces away.
items.e: Then deposition.

items.q: Which happened first: oxygen begins to build up in the air, or the first microbial fossils (stromatolites)?
c: They happened at the same time.
oxygen begins to build up in the air
items.e: The first microbial fossils (stromatolites): about 3.5 billion years ago; oxygen begins to build up in the air: about 2.4 billion years ago.

items.q: Why are the Earth's resources such as metal ores limited?
c: They are made again every year.
They took millions of years to form and are being used much faster.
items.e: Finite resources.

items.q: Which rock forms when limestone is heated and squeezed?
items.e: Limestone is metamorphosed into marble.

items.q: Which of these is an igneous rock: limestone, marble, obsidian or slate?
items.e: Igneous rock is formed when hot, melted rock cools and hardens.

items.q: In which kind of rock are fossils usually found?
items.e: Sediments bury dead organisms gently.

items.q: Does the rock cycle always happen in the same order?
c: No. Any rock can change into any other type by different paths.
items.e: It is a cycle with many paths.

items.q: What kind of rock is Kata Tjuta made of?
items.e: It formed from rounded pebbles and boulders cemented together.

items.q: Why does granite have large crystals but basalt has small ones?
c: Granite cooled slowly underground; basalt cooled quickly at the surface.
Crystals grow faster at the surface.
items.e: Slow cooling gives time for large crystals to grow.

items.q: Layer C has a dinosaur footprint fossil. What does this tell you about the area when layer C formed?
c: The area has always looked the same.
The area was always covered by ice.
The area was once dry land with plants or animals living on it.
The area was once covered by water.
items.e: A dinosaur footprint fossil is evidence that the area was once dry land with plants or animals living on it.

items.q: How do sedimentary rocks form?
c: layers of sediment are deposited, compacted and cemented
items.e: Sandstone and limestone are sedimentary.

items.q: Which process turns loose sand into sandstone?
items.e: Minerals in water glue the grains together.

items.q: A geologist finds a rock with bands of crystals and no fossils. Which type is it most likely to be?
items.e: Banding forms under pressure.

items.q: Which of these is NOT a fossil: a chicken bone from last night's dinner, a fern leaf print in shale, a fish skeleton pressed into stone or a sea urchin made of flint?
c: a chicken bone from last night's dinner
a fish skeleton pressed into stone
a sea urchin made of flint
a fern leaf print in shale
items.e: A chicken bone from last night's dinner is not the preserved remains of a living thing from millions of years ago.

items.q: Why is granite used for kitchen benches?
c: It is hard, strong and resists scratching.
items.e: Igneous rocks with interlocking crystals are hard.

items.q: Diane drops dilute acid on a rock and it fizzes. What does this suggest?
c: The rock contains calcium carbonate, such as limestone or marble.
items.e: Carbonates react with acid to make carbon dioxide.

items.q: Is sandstone an igneous, sedimentary or metamorphic rock?
items.e: Sedimentary rock is formed from layers of sand, mud or shells pressed together.

items.q: How do igneous rocks form?
c: when rocks are heated and squeezed without melting
when layers of sediment are pressed together
when magma or lava cools and becomes solid
items.e: Granite and basalt are igneous.

items.q: Nico soaks four rocks of the same size in water and weighs them before and after. Which result shows the most porous rock?
c: the rock with the biggest increase in mass
items.e: Porous rocks soak up water.

items.q: How do metamorphic rocks form?
c: existing rocks are changed by heat and pressure without melting
items.e: Marble and slate are metamorphic.

items.q: Which of these is a fossil: a chicken bone from last night's dinner, a crystal of quartz, a piece of brick or a trilobite in a slab of rock?
c: a trilobite in a slab of rock
a chicken bone from last night's dinner
items.e: A fossil is the remains or trace of a living thing from long ago, preserved in rock.

items.q: Which of these is a sedimentary rock: basalt, chalk, granite or marble?
items.e: Sedimentary rock is formed from layers of sand, mud or shells pressed together.

items.q: Which of these is NOT a fossil: a dinosaur footprint in rock, a plastic toy dinosaur, a shark tooth found in chalk or an ammonite shell turned to stone?
c: an ammonite shell turned to stone
a shark tooth found in chalk
items.e: A plastic toy dinosaur is not the preserved remains of a living thing from millions of years ago.

items.q: Jomar finds a rock that forms when existing rock is changed by heat and pressure without melting. What type of rock is it?
items.e: Metamorphic rock forms when existing rock is changed by heat and pressure without melting.

items.q: Renz's model shows sedimentary rock changing into metamorphic rock. Which process causes this?
c: weathering, erosion, deposition, then compaction and cementation
items.e: In the rock cycle, sedimentary rock becomes metamorphic rock by heat and pressure deep underground.

items.q: What are the three main types of rock?
items.e: They form in different ways.

items.q: Rose's model shows igneous rock changing into sedimentary rock. Which process causes this?
c: weathering, erosion, deposition, then compaction and cementation
items.e: In the rock cycle, igneous rock becomes sedimentary rock by weathering, erosion, deposition, then compaction and cementation.

items.q: Jenny needs an igneous rock for a display. Which sample should Jenny choose?
items.e: Igneous rocks include granite, basalt, obsidian, pumice.

items.q: Hazel asks what energy source drives rivers carrying sediment downhill in the rock cycle. What is the best answer?
items.e: Interior heat drives melting and metamorphism; the sun drives weathering and erosion.

items.q: Diane's model shows metamorphic rock changing into igneous rock. Which process causes this?
c: weathering, erosion, deposition, then compaction and cementation
items.e: In the rock cycle, metamorphic rock becomes igneous rock by melting into magma, then cooling.

items.q: What is the rock cycle?
c: the slow processes that change rocks from one type to another
the path of a rolling rock
items.e: Rocks are constantly recycled over millions of years.

items.q: Trisha asks what energy source drives metamorphism (heat and pressure) in the rock cycle. What is the best answer?
c: the sun (which drives the water cycle)
items.e: Interior heat drives melting and metamorphism; the sun drives weathering and erosion.

items.q: Which rock type often contains fossils?

items.q: Isabel's rock kit has a sample of gneiss. What type of rock is it?

items.q: Rafael needs a metamorphic rock for a display. Which sample should Rafael choose?

items.q: Can a rock follow different paths through the rock cycle?
c: No, there is only one path.
Yes. Any rock type can become any other type.
items.e: The cycle has many paths.

items.q: A mountain range rises 4 mm per year. How much higher would it be after 100,000 years (ignoring erosion)? (1 km = 1,000,000 mm)
Why is a cap rock needed for an oil or gas reservoir?
c: it is impermeable, so it stops the oil and gas escaping upwards
items.e: Shale and salt are common cap rocks.

items.q: Iron in rocks reacts with water and oxygen and turns red-brown. Which type of weathering is this?
items.e: Physical weathering breaks rock into pieces; chemical weathering changes the minerals.

items.q: Ice forms in a crack and splits a boulder. Which type of weathering is this?
items.e: Physical weathering breaks rock into pieces; chemical weathering changes the minerals.

items.q: Miguel's model: a mountain is uplifted 4 mm per year and eroded 0.2 mm per year. How much does its height change in 1,000,000 years?
Patricia reads about a resource that formed from iron that settled out of ancient oceans in layers. Which resource is it?
items.e: That is how iron ore formed.

items.q: Feldspar in granite slowly changes into clay in wet soil. Which type of weathering is this?
items.e: Physical weathering breaks rock into pieces; chemical weathering changes the minerals.

items.q: Why can a deposit that was not ore become ore?
c: the deposit moves closer to the surface
a rise in metal price or a cheaper mining method makes it profitable
the metal grows in the rock
items.e: Economics defines ore.

items.q: A river cuts down into rock 1 mm per year. How deep will its canyon be after 2,000,000 years? (1 m = 1,000 mm)
Rainwater with CO₂ dissolves a marble statue. Which type of weathering is this?
items.e: Physical weathering breaks rock into pieces; chemical weathering changes the minerals.

items.q: A river erodes downward 0.5 mm per year. About how long would it take to cut a canyon 1,500 m deep?
Jasmine asks how iron ore formed. What is the best explanation?
c: from plants from ancient swamps buried and squeezed for millions of years
from tiny marine organisms buried in ocean sediments, then heated and pressed for millions of years
from iron that settled out of ancient oceans in layers
from seawater evaporating in shallow basins long ago
items.e: Iron ore formed from iron that settled out of ancient oceans in layers.

items.q: What is an artesian aquifer?
c: a confined aquifer in which pressure pushes water up a bore without pumping
items.e: It is trapped between impermeable layers.

items.q: How do oil and natural gas form?
c: remains of marine plankton are buried, heated and changed into hydrocarbons, which collect in traps
items.e: They need a source rock, reservoir rock and cap rock.

items.q: When is open-cut mining used rather than underground mining?
c: when the ore is large and close to the surface
when the ore is very deep and narrow
items.e: The Super Pit at Kalgoorlie is open-cut.

items.q: A river cuts down into rock 1 mm per year. How deep will its canyon be after 100,000 years? (1 m = 1,000 mm)
A river cuts down into rock 2 mm per year. How deep will its canyon be after 500,000 years? (1 m = 1,000 mm)
Why are fossil fuels called non-renewable?
c: they form over millions of years, far slower than we use them
they are found only in deserts
items.e: Coal, oil and gas are non-renewable.

items.q: A mountain range rises 2 mm per year. How much higher would it be after 100,000 years (ignoring erosion)? (1 km = 1,000,000 mm)
What is groundwater?
c: water stored in pores and fractures of rock and sediment below the water table
items.e: Aquifers store groundwater.
